To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the flow regime in a drinking water contact tanks can change between laminar and turbulent flow, (2) the flow regime can affect the disinfection efficacy of the system, (3) the flow regime of the system can be altered by changing inlet conditions, and (4) the flow regime is not affected by the flow rate of water in the contact tank.
a drinking water contact storage tank with an annual flow regime change from laminary to turbulent flow can be stabilized with proper inlet modification.
the BF of the contact tank can be improved by changing the inlet geometry to a 90-degree elbow and that the flow regime can be maintained at the desired level by changing the flow rate.

the development of CFD models for drinking water contact tanks and the use of these models to study flow regimes and to investigate inlet modifications to stabilize the BF of the tank.
the flow regime of a water contact tank and the effects of inlet modification on the flow pattern of the system.
the effects of flow regimes on drinking water contact tanks, which can affect the performance of the system.

a CFD model of a drinking water treatment contact tank can be used to determine the flow regime, and inlet modifications can be used to maintain the desired flow regime.

the flow regime of the system can be altered to improve the disinfection efficiency by modifying the inlet geometry of the tank.

the CFD model is a valuable tool to investigate and improve the performance of drinking water contact tanks and that a regime change from laminary to turbulent flow (and vice versa) can significantly affect the disinfectant efficiency of the contact tank.

the inlet design can be used as a tool to stabilize the BF of a drinking water system.
the flow regime can significantly influence disinfection efficiency in drinking water contact systems.
